messages.body_plain:
Jürgen, I think this is likely a bug in ggvis. I believe that the hovering event handlers aren't being set up properly when a new plot spec is sent to the client. In any case, there's also a subtle but important difference between this app and ones that are auto-generated by ggvis. First, a little background. In Vega (the rendering engine) and ggvis, there are two separate pieces: the spec, which is a declarative grammar-of-graphics description of the plot, and the data. You can change the data without forcing a complete recomputation and redraw of the plot; however, if you change the spec, the plot must be completely redrawn. In this app you're using shiny::sliderInput, and reading the value in a reactive expression with input$size. Whenever that value changes, the reactive expression is invalidated, and is run again. This runs the ggvis() function call again, and the result is that a new spec and data is sent to the client. When you change the slider, you'll see the whole plot blink, which indicates that a new spec is being used. Below I've included a modified version of your app. Instead of using shiny::sliderInput, it uses ggvis::input_slider, which is wrapper around sliderInput that returns a _delayed_ reactive object. Notice that this version of the app doesn't refer to input$size or anything like that. Because of this, the reactive expression isn't invalidated when the slider value changes, and it doesn't get re-executed, and a new spec is not sent to the client - only new data. You won't see the blink when you change the slider values with this app. Also, the tooltips will keep working. (Sorry if this sounds a little opaque -- I'd have to revisit that code in order to give a good description of how delayed reactives are handled behind the scenes.) A slightly tweaked version of your original app: ======================================== library(shiny) library(ggvis) server <- function(input, output, session) { all_values <- function(x) { if(is.null(x)) return(NULL) paste0(names(x), ": ", format(x), collapse = "
") } gv <- reactive({ ggvis(mtcars, props(x = ~disp, y = ~mpg, size := input$size)) + tooltip(all_values) + layer_point() }) observe_ggvis(gv, "my_plot", session) } ui <- pageWithSidebar( headerPanel(""), sidebarPanel( sliderInput("size", "Area", 10, 1000,20) ), mainPanel( ggvis_output("my_plot") ) ) runApp(list(server=server, ui=ui)) ======================================== And here's my version of it using ggvis::input_slider: ======================================== library(shiny) library(ggvis) server <- function(input, output, session) { all_values <- function(x) { if(is.null(x)) return(NULL) paste0(names(x), ": ", format(x), collapse = "
") } gv <- reactive({ size_slider <- input_slider(label = "Area", 10, 1000, 20) ggvis(mtcars, props(x = ~disp, y = ~mpg, size := size_slider)) + tooltip(all_values) + layer_point() }) observe_ggvis(gv, "my_plot", session) output$ggvis_controls <- renderControls(gv, session) } ui <- pageWithSidebar( headerPanel(""), sidebarPanel( ggvisControlOutput("ggvis_controls", "my_plot") ), mainPanel( ggvis_output("my_plot") ) ) runApp(list(server=server, ui=ui)) ======================================== Hope this helps! -Winston On Sat, Mar 1, 2014 at 11:44 PM, Familie Gieshoff wrote: > Dear all, > > the tooltip ability of ggvis in a shiny app is lost after updating the graph with another point size through the sliderInput. > The code delivers the plot in the web browser (Firefox 27.0.1) w/o problems. > > Best regards, > Jürgen > > The code: > > shinyServer(function(input, output, session) { > all_values <- function(x) { > if(is.null(x)) return(NULL) > paste0(names(x), ": ", format(x), collapse = "

Hi Ramnath -

Hm, that error message isn't very informative. Do you mind filing an issue on that?

In ggplot2, grouping is done automatically if a discrete variable in the data is mapped to an aesthetic. When calculating transforms (like smooth), the data is split apart into pieces, and the transform is applied to each piece.

In ggvis (as of now) the grouping doesn't happen automatically when a variable in the data is mapped to a property. So in the layer_smooth, it's trying to calculate a single model line from all the data, but also map the cut variable for each point to the stroke color -- and those two things won't work together.

Here are two ways of doing this. (I'm also taking a subset of the diamonds data set, since there are some to-be-addressed bottlenecks that cause slow rendering for ~53k points.)

data('diamonds', package='ggplot2')
d <- diamonds[sample(nrow(diamonds), 1000), ]

# In this version, the grouping on cut is done for all layers, although it's
# only visible for the layer_smooth
ggvis(diamond, by_group(cut), props(x = ~carat, y = ~price)) +

  layer_point(props(opacity := 0.5)) +
  layer_smooth(props(stroke = ~cut))

# In this version, the grouping on cut is done only for the layer_smooth
ggvis(d, props(x = ~carat, y = ~price)) +
  layer_point(props(opacity := 0.5)) +
  layer(
    by_group(cut),
    layer_smooth(props(stroke = ~cut))
  )

One thing we want to do for the future is to make the grouping simpler to use.

-Winston

      opts(width = 300, height = 300)

Hi Ian -

It looks like there's a bug in creating the legend section of the spec. This _should_ work, but doesn't:

ggvis(mtcars, props(x =~ mpg, y =~ disp, fill =~ factor(cyl), size =~ hp)) +
  layer_point() +

  guide_legend("size", properties = list(legend = props(y := 150)))

The problem is that in the spec, there should be a section that looks like this:
"legends" : [
  {
    "size" : "size",
    "orient" : "right",
    "properties" : {
      "legend" : {
        "y" : {
          "value" : 100
        }
      }
    },
    "title" : "hp"
  },
 ...
]

But instead the "properties" subsection looks like this, with an extra "update" in there:
  "properties" : {
    "legend" : {
      "update" : {
        "y" : {
          "value" : 150
        }
      }
    }
  }

Until it's fixed, if you're bold enough to edit the HTML output directly, you can remove the "update" layer in the JSON object.

Also, if you're looking at the plots in RStudio and find that it always points to a localhost address instead of directly to a file, you can use this to see the URL:
p <- ggvis(mtcars, props(x =~ mpg, y =~ disp, fill =~ factor(cyl), size =~ hp)) +
  layer_point() +
  guide_legend("size", properties = list(legend = props(y := 150)))
file <- print(p, launch = FALSE)
browseURL(file)

-Winston

>           "value" : 150
>         }
>       }
>     }
>   }
